views.name: Step 1
views.caption: Begin the controller with the controller board, printed side down. Press the left guard onto the half of the board with the L-JS socket.
views.review: How do the guards go on? The CAD has each as a tray under one half of the board (here pressed on with the board face down); your photo shows four rim pieces. And should they go on first, as here? Names to confirm: Controller Board, Left / Right Controller Guard, Nano Board, Radio Module, Joystick, USB Cable, Nano I/O Module, Adapter Board, Wheel Motor, Wheel, 9V Battery, Battery Clip.

views.name: Step 5
views.caption: Set the left joystick into its pocket, then push it towards L-JS until its pins are all the way into the socket.
views.review: In the CAD the joystick's board overlaps the controller board at the end away from its socket (the cut-out is 31.6 mm, the joystick 34 mm): by 4 mm when it is in, 11 mm while it is set down short of its socket here, and its underside sits 2.8 mm into the guard's floor. How does the joystick really sit? And do its pins go into the top row of L-JS (as in the CAD)? If so, a caution here would say so.

views.name: Step 7
views.caption: Begin the car's electronics with the I/O module. Press the other Nano Board into it, its USB socket at the same end as the power socket.
views.review: The published guide shows this Nano Board the other way round (USB socket towards the front); the CAD and the MRA have it at the power socket's end, as here. And the CAD's Nano Board here is a plainer model, so the controller's Nano Board is shown instead. Colours to confirm (materials.json _notes.unconfirmed): the wheel motors' blue (as published, or black?), the radio boards black or green, the wheels, the plug housings, silver or gold pins, the white boards; and is this I/O module the MRA's board (its printing is carried over)?

views.caption: Plug the left wheel motor into LWh for the test. Remember brown to G, red to V, and yellow to S.
views.review: The CAD and the published guide draw the signal wire yellow (the MRA's captions say orange): which is it on the kit's FS90R? And how long is the lead? The CAD's two poses of each lead differ (71 mm loose, 110 / 165 mm plugged); both are drawn 115 mm here.
views.caution: Very important: the brown wire goes on G, the pin on the same side as the left wheel.

views.name: Step 17
views.caption:
Testing Checklist
Go through the following checklist to make sure you have tested each part of your RCC:
•  The controller was powered on by connecting a Mini-USB cable to its Nano.
•  The car was powered on by plugging in the 9V battery.
•  Pushing the left joystick forward made the left wheel turn.
•  Pushing the right joystick forward made the right wheel turn.
•  Each wheel stopped when its joystick was released.
•  The battery was unplugged and the Mini-USB cable disconnected after testing.
views.review: A placeholder: TechBox's RCC Testing Checklist is needed word for word, as for the MRA. Which joystick drives which wheel? Does the FS90R's stop trim need setting during the test?
